key_insight: AtomWorld-Mirror replaces slow event-by-event atomistic simulation with a time-aware macro-step world model that predicts key structural transitions and elapsed physical time in one step.
engineering_relevance: This could dramatically accelerate long-horizon materials-dynamics studies, helping engineers explore diffusion, defects, interfacial reactions, and fracture much faster while preserving physically valid evolution.
method: Distills short micro-event segments into latent macro-step transitions between key states
Jointly predicts sparse structural edits and accumulated physical time
Enforces local reachability, inventory conservation, and continuous-time consistency
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation across five atomic systems, including Cu-rich RPV steel, Cu-Zr metallic glass, and Li3N-based anti-perovskite electrolyte, with 10^3 to 10^4× speedups over event-by-event simulation.
watch_item: The approach depends on learning a reusable latent macro-model, so accuracy and generalization may be sensitive to the training data coverage and the physical constraints enforced.
paper_title: AtomWorld-Mirror: Macro-Step World Modeling of Critical Evolution Backbones for Materials Dynamics
